reads.stopped_at: It does not establish how Repairboard would fit an existing process or whether updates require separate entry.
reads.what_it_sells: Repairboard appears to be a shared digital repair-status board that would let me show customers each repair’s current stage through a read-only link.
reads.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly says I am considering how customers can inspect repair stages, and the email offers a read-only customer view of those stages, so the premise fits. The email additionally presupposes that a shared board may suit my shop; whether it fits my current workflow, customer communication habits, or update process remains unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am considering ways for customers to inspect repair stages.
Email-only: My shop could use a shared board as the place where repair status is presented.
Email-only: I may be willing to send customers read-only status links.
Unknown: How I currently record repairs or communicate status updates.
Unknown: Whether Repairboard would require duplicate entry or connect to an existing process.
reads.problem_now: Customer inspection of repair stages is explicitly relevant, but no urgency, current failure, or implementation deadline is established. The immediate question is whether this presentation method is suitable, not whether I need to replace an existing system now.
reads.biggest_doubt: The email raises the exact operational concern that matters—whether staff would have to enter updates separately—but does not answer it. I do not want to spend even a short break inspecting a display if maintaining it may create duplicate work.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me whether viewing the sample requires a login and whether Repairboard can avoid separate status entry—or clearly said that the sample takes under a minute and only evaluates the customer view.
fixes: Rewrite “It does not establish how Repairboard would fit an existing process or whether updates require separate entry.” as “The sample shows only the customer view; it does not show whether Repairboard connects to your current process or requires separate updates.”

Rewrite “For now, it offers one useful test: whether this way of presenting repair stages suits how you want customers to inspect status.” as “Open the sample to see exactly what a customer would see from a read-only repair-status link.”
Rewrite “View the sample repair board →” to specify the immediate effort and access requirement, such as “View the read-only sample board—no login required →” only if that claim is true.
